newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes fall in thin pre-weekend talk.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes fall in thin pre-weekend talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices slid Friday, tracking a sharp decline in WTI/Cushing prices with local trade limited ahead of the weekend, traders said.
NYMEX March crude fell 87 cents to $22.23 a barrel.
Following the sale of two Alaskan crude cargoes earlier this week, four to five refiners still needed to purchase barrels for March, traders said.
The two Alaskan cargoes sold at $1.30 and $1.18 a barrel under March WTI.
California posted price fell 50 cents a barrel overnight on the heals of steep declines in NYMEX.
Wilmington's average price fell to $17.78, off 65 cents from last week, while Kern River was down about 60 cents to $16.81 a barrel.
About 1.2 million extra barrels of heavy crudes continued to pressure California markets after Tosco's damaged refinery declared force majeure on deliveries last week.
Texaco, a key heavy crude producer in Calif., was reported to own the bulk of the turned-back crude, with 30,000 of the 40,000 barrels-per-day declined by Tosco, traders said.
Confirmed prices for San Joaquin Valley heavies ranged $16.31 to 16.56 a barrel.
